name: Yorkrakine Rock
reason: Rule 1-2: Australia's Golden Outback Tammin page names it (25 km north of Tammin, access road, picnic facilities, birdwatching, walk trail to gnamma holes on top) and Wheatbelt Tourism's Eastern Wheatbelt self-drive trail features it; a granite summit walk is a half-hour-plus visit.
objection: One of dozens of similar Wheatbelt granite outcrops; a visitor would mostly stop if passing on the Wheatbelt Way.

name: Yeerakine Rock
reason: Rule 1-2: Wheatbelt Tourism (Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre) lists it under Granite Outcrops (12 km south of Kondinin, summit views, Roe's 1848 camp, Light Horse silhouette statue); the Golden Outback Kondinin page also names it; a summit walk with picnic area.
objection: Second-tier rock near a small town; only one counted page was opened (wheatbelttourism.com), the Golden Outback mention is from search.

name: Gnarlbine Rock
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Gnarlbine Rock/Soak, 30 km SW of Coolgardie on the Holland Track, appears only in the heritage register and blogs.
objection: A historic gold-rush soak with camp sites on the Holland Track; a Goldfields guide or the Coolgardie visitor page might list it: worth one more look by the proposer.

name: Yardina Rock
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 No visitor information exists for it at all.
objection: None found.

name: Yakkan Toort (Dog Rock)
reason: outside the region: belongs to wa-great-southern (the coordinates -35.019, 117.886 are Dog Rock on Middleton Road, Albany, not a Wheatbelt rock; the candidate's note is wrong).
objection: Dog Rock is a well-known Albany roadside icon: the Great Southern pass should have it.

name: Lake Campion
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage's Wheatbelt page names it ('a great salt-encrusted lake' NE of Nungarin): one counted source.
objection: A one-line mention with no access point, facilities or walk named; a salt lake seen from the road may not give half an hour. Needs a second source (e.g. Wheatbelt Way trail map) to keep.

name: PUBLIC Silo Art Trail
reason: Not a place (COVERAGE 'A spot is a place'): a trail of painted silos across many towns; each silo (Merredin CBH silos, Ravensthorpe silos) is the place and should be judged as its own candidate.
objection: The silos are a genuine draw; make sure Merredin and Ravensthorpe silos are candidates on their own.

name: Wheatbelt Way
reason: Not a place: a multi-day self-drive route through the northern Wheatbelt; its stops (rocks, lakes, towns) are the spots.
objection: Board-promoted, but a route has no single point to visit.

name: Great Victoria Desert
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 It is a vast desert region with no visitor point; not a spot (rule 2: nothing to do at a place).
objection: High page views; a desert crossing (Anne Beadell or Great Central Road) is a known 4WD trip, but the place visitors stop at would be a named site, not the whole desert.

name: Lake Johnston
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Only campsite listings on the Hyden-Norseman Road.
objection: A free camp and salt-lake stop on the Hyden-Norseman road that travellers do use.

name: Lake Carnegie
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Remote ephemeral salt lake with no visitor access.
objection: None of note.

name: Lake Wells
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Remote salt lake, no visitor access.
objection: None of note.

name: Lake Darlot
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Remote salt lake near Leinster/Wiluna, no visitor access.
objection: None of note.

name: Lake Gore
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Ramsar wetland west of Esperance with no visitor facilities named; Esperance's visitor lake is Lake Monjingup.
objection: Ramsar-listed bird site; birders do go.

name: Lake Hopkins
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Remote salt lake on Ngaanyatjarra lands (permits).
objection: None of note.

name: Serpentine Lakes
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Remote salt lakes on the WA/SA border in the Great Victoria Desert, reached only by 4WD expedition.
objection: On the Anne Beadell Highway route; expedition travellers pass it.

name: Shark Lake
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 A nature reserve 13 km north of Esperance; no visitor source names facilities or a reason to go.
objection: A permanent freshwater wetland near Esperance; a local guide might list it.

name: Yeo Lake
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Remote salt lake in a nature reserve, no visitor access.
objection: None of note.

name: Toolibin Lake
reason: Rule 1-2: the DBCA Explore Parks page for Toolibin Nature Reserve invites birdwatchers and bushwalkers and describes the 1.6 km, 45-minute Recovery Walk loop with interpretive signs (also on Trails WA); Ramsar-listed lake with 41 waterbird species.
objection: The lake rarely fills, the walk trail closes when it is full, and DBCA asks visitors to contact the Narrogin office first: a niche birding stop.

name: Wagin Lake
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Only a naturalists' trip note and a local news story about a bird hide.
objection: Now has a bird hide and car park; Wagin's draws are the Giant Ram and Historical Village.

name: Lake Yealering
reason: Rule 1-2: the Shire of Wickepin's Explore page names it (picnic area, BBQs, walk trail round the banks, kayaking, sailing and skiing when full, black swans, astrophotography) and Australia's Golden Outback describes it similarly.
objection: An ephemeral town lake used mainly for local recreation; fails the friend test unless already nearby, and is often dry.

name: Lake Grace South
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 The visitor point for the Lake Grace system is the Lake Grace Lookout (a separate listing on the board).
objection: Possible near-duplicate of a Lake Grace lookout candidate.

name: Lake Towerrinning
reason: Rule 1-2: the Shire of West Arthur's lake page (the reserve is vested in the shire) describes water sports including skiing, BBQs, picnic shelters, a boardwalk, a playground and 128 bird species; a private campground adjoins it.
objection: A local water-ski and camping lake 32 km south of Darkan; no tourism-board or guidebook page was found, so it may be a place mostly locals use.

name: Lake Baandee
reason: Rule 2/4 and 1: Wheatbelt Tourism only notes it as a gazetted water-ski area when full, depending on the season; nothing to see or do when dry, and no visitor facility named.
objection: On the Great Eastern Highway east of Kellerberrin, so many pass it; the board does mention it.

name: Jilakin Lake
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Kulin page lists 'Jilakin Lake and Rock': views from the top of Jilakin Rock, picnics under the most inland stand of jarrah, the Bush Races track, and a spring wildflower site. A rock climb and lake picnic is a half-hour-plus visit. Better named 'Jilakin Rock' (the rock is the visitor point; pin the rock).
objection: Only one counted source; a second-tier stop near Kulin.

name: Yenyening Lakes
reason: Rule 1: two counted sources, Australia's Golden Outback product page and Wheatbelt Tourism's Granite Outcrops & Salt Lakes page (birdlife, water sports, photography). Boundary unsure: 32 km SE of Beverley, spanning the Beverley, Brookton and Quairading shires; Beverley is in wa-perth's Avon Valley.
objection: Salt lakes that need generous rain to fill; mainly a local recreation spot; may belong to wa-perth.

name: Lake Cronin
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Only ExplorOz/community listings: a 4WD sandy-track day-use stop off the Hyden-Norseman road.
objection: The region's largest freshwater lake and a birding stop for overlanders.

name: Lake Magenta
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 A remote nature reserve with no visitor facilities named.
objection: None of note.

name: Parkeyerring Lake
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1
objection: None of note.

name: Dumbleyung Lake
reason: Rule 1-2: Australia's Golden Outback has a product page (Lake Dumbleyung, where Donald Campbell set the 1964 water speed record in Bluebird; the scenic drive up Pussy Cat Hill to the Campbell memorial and view over the largest inland water body in the south-west; boating, swimming, skiing, birdwatching), plus the Dumbleyung town page.
objection: The water level varies, and the strongest draw may be the Bluebird replica in Dumbleyung town; the pin should be Pussy Cat Hill lookout.

name: Gill Pinnacle
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 A remote inselberg on Ngaanyatjarra lands near Warburton (permit area); the note's 'Wheatbelt' is wrong.
objection: None of note.

name: Badjaling Nature Reserve
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 No walk or facilities; Quairading's visitor reserves are Nookaminnie Rock and Pink Lake.
objection: None of note.

name: Charles Darwin Reserve
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Perenjori page names it (a Bush Heritage reserve of national ecological significance, 230 animal and 680 plant species, camping June-September at Samphire Campground, booked through Bush Heritage); Bush Heritage also runs guided visits.
objection: Open only by booking in a limited season (sources disagree: Apr-Oct or Jun-Sep); one counted source. Boundary unsure: the Shire of Perenjori is administratively Mid West, next to the coral-coast wildflower towns (Morawa, Three Springs), though the Golden Outback brand lists it under the Wheatbelt.

name: Spider Orchard Wongan Hills
reason: Not a place: 'Spider Orchard' is a photo caption (a typo for spider orchid) on the Golden Outback Wongan Hills page; the wildflower places it names are Reynoldson's and Gathercole reserves and the Mount Matilda walk, which are the candidates to judge.
objection: Wongan Hills wildflowers are a real draw; check that Reynoldson's Flora Reserve is a candidate.

name: Kulin
reason: Town rule: Australia's Golden Outback gives Kulin its own page as 'the perfect base to explore the Eastern Wheatbelt', with the Tin Horse Highway, the Discovery Zone, the giant waterslide, Jilakin Rock and Buckley's Breakaway around it.
objection: Its main draw (the Tin Horse Highway) is a separate keep, so a Kulin town spot risks being a wrapper around it (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); the proposer may better use it as a base/destination name.

name: Corrigin
reason: Town rule: the Golden Outback Corrigin page gives it its own section as 'a popular stopover' on the way to Wave Rock: 'Town of Windmills', Pioneer Museum, Corrigin Rock and ANZAC lookouts, the Dog Cemetery, Gorge Rock and the Wildflower Drive.
objection: The best-known sight (Dog Cemetery) is a separate keep, so the town could be a wrapper; it is a stopover more than a base.

name: Southern Cross
reason: Town rule: the Golden Outback Southern Cross page gives it a section: a Golden Pipeline town on the Great Eastern Highway with the Yilgarn History Museum (open daily), Wimmera Hill Lookout, the pioneer cemetery and star-named streets, and accommodation; a stop between Perth and Kalgoorlie.
objection: Mainly a highway stop; its museum is a separate keep.

name: Sandstone
reason: Town rule: the Golden Outback Sandstone page gives it a section: gold-rush town with restored heritage buildings, the Sandstone Heritage Trail, the museum and visitor centre, London Bridge, the Peter Denny Lookout, and accommodation.
objection: Very remote and small; its headline sight, London Bridge, is a separate keep.

name: Tin Horse Highway
reason: Rule 1-3: a quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE names these as spots): Australia's Golden Outback has a product page (over 70 tin horses along about 15 km of road to the Jilakin race track, 'a quirky open-air gallery') and the Kulin page calls it the town's famous draw.
objection: A stretch of road rather than a point; pin it at the middle of the stretch. A drive-through of about 20 minutes, though people stop to photograph each horse.

name: West Kulin Tin Horses
reason: Rule 3: part of a larger spot: the tin horses on the western side of Kulin are 'an introduction to the Tin Horse Highway' (Golden Outback Kulin page), which is kept.
objection: None; mention them in the Tin Horse Highway bio.

name: Kulin Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Kulin page names it (Butler's Garage, one of Kulin's original buildings, with vintage cars, farm equipment and machinery).
objection: Open only on Saturday mornings and by appointment, so most visitors arrive to find it shut; one source; a small local museum.

name: Buckley's Breakaway
reason: Rule 1-3: the Golden Outback Kulin page names it as a picnic spot and 'a photographer's delight': orange clays against white cliffs and gullies, also a spring wildflower spot. A second-tier natural stop a real source names.
objection: One counted source only; no coordinates in the candidate, and the access is not described.

name: Kulin Giant Waterslide and Aquatic Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Kulin page names it as one of the three things Kulin is famous for ('regional Australia's biggest waterslide'); it is a seasonal venue (summer), which is allowed.
objection: It is the town's public swimming pool, a council facility mostly used by locals; one source.

name: Corrigin Dog Cemetery
reason: Rule 1-3: a quirky roadside icon with its own Australia's Golden Outback product page and a mention on the Corrigin page: a pet cemetery founded in 1974 with over 200 dogs, marked by a large dog statue, 5 km west of town on the Brookton Highway.
objection: A short stop (15-30 minutes); both counted mentions are from one board.

name: Corrigin Pioneer Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Corrigin page and its Dog Cemetery page name it (restored farm machinery, a pioneers' memorial wall).
objection: A small local museum with no hours found; one board only.

name: Corrigin Rock
reason: Rule 1: re-look found it named on the Golden Outback Corrigin page ('Take a walk up Corrigin Rock' for sunrise or sunset views of the town and farmland).
objection: A short lookout walk on a town outcrop, one passing mention; may be a 15-minute stop.

name: Dog in a Ute Statue
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Only an aggregator (Visit Wanderland) mentions the chainsaw dog sculpture for the 2002 dogs-in-utes record; rule 3 also: a small statue, minor next to the Dog Cemetery.
objection: A fun photo stop tied to Corrigin's world record; could be mentioned in the Corrigin bio.

name: London Bridge
reason: Rule 1-3: two Golden Outback pages (its own product page: a 350-million-year-old natural rock arch 3 km south of Sandstone, a picnic and sunset spot for over 100 years, 'one of Sandstone's most iconic sights', dark-sky photography; and the Heritage Trail page). A distinct natural feature a guide singles out, not just a trail stop. DATA ERROR: the candidate's coordinates (51.508, -0.088) and 370,378 page views are London Bridge in England; re-resolve the pin near Sandstone (wiki 'London Bridge (Western Australia)' if it exists) and set views from the right article.
objection: A short visit (15-30 minutes) unless staying for sunset; it is one stop on the Sandstone Heritage Trail.

name: Sandstone Heritage Trail
reason: Not a place: an 18 km self-drive (plus town walk) linking Sandstone's buildings, London Bridge and the brewery site; its stops are judged separately (London Bridge kept) and the town (Sandstone, kept) covers the rest, so this is a duplicate of Sandstone.
objection: The board promotes it as a half-day outing, and the walking tours with a local guide are a real experience; the bio of Sandstone should mention it.

name: Sandstone Heritage Museum and Visitor Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Sandstone page names it (a small heritage museum attached to the visitor centre, gold-rush and pastoral memorabilia; it holds the key to the Black Range Chapel and its stained glass).
objection: Small, inside a visitor centre; one board; perhaps a 20-minute visit.

name: Tjukurba Art Gallery
reason: Rule 1-2: two counted sources: the Golden Outback Wiluna page (historic photos and paintings by Martu artists who work in the gallery workshop) and the Shire of Wiluna tourism page ('a must', a working gallery where visitors meet the artists). Aboriginal art centre, a cultural draw.
objection: Partly a shop selling works; hours not found; small. Spelling varies (Tjukurba / Tjurkurba / Tjkurba).

name: Canning-Gunbarrel Discovery Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: two counted sources: the Golden Outback Wiluna page and the Shire of Wiluna tourism page (a museum in the restored old hospital on Wiluna's history, the Canning Stock Route and the Gunbarrel Highway; where travellers get the town map).
objection: Part visitor centre; modest in size.

name: Wiluna Red Hill Lookout
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Wiluna page names Red Hill Lookout, a rocky rise 1.2 km south of town with views over Wiluna to the gold mine.
objection: One source; a short lookout over a mine; probably under half an hour.

name: Wiluna Clay Pans
reason: Rule 4: only worth visiting after rain, when they fill (Golden Outback Wiluna page); not there whenever a visitor arrives, and only one passing mention.
objection: After rain they are a birding and picnic spot.

name: Wiluna North Pool
reason: Rule 1-2: two counted sources: the Shire of Wiluna tourism page (a peaceful waterhole 15 km out among red earth and gum trees, for a picnic, walk or sunset) and the Golden Outback Wiluna page (camping at North Pool). A second-tier natural stop.
objection: A local swimming/picnic waterhole; unofficial camping; access is on unsealed roads.

name: Last of the Nomads Statue
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Wiluna page names it and tells its story at length (Warri and Yatungka, believed the last desert nomads, found in 1977); at the town entrance.
objection: A statue is a short photo stop and could fail rule 3 as a minor memorial; one source.

name: Wiluna Pioneer Cemetery
reason: Rule 3: a minor heritage site given one line ('view the grave sites... 1893 to 1903') on the Golden Outback Wiluna page; not a draw a visitor goes out of their way for.
objection: None of note.

name: Wiluna Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Wiluna, the town: a brochure walk around the town is how the town itself is seen, and belongs in the town's entry, not a separate spot (one source).
objection: Heritage walks are sometimes listed as spots; if Wiluna itself is not kept, this would be the way to represent it.

name: Yilgarn History Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Australia's Golden Outback has a product page: the museum in Southern Cross's 1892 courthouse (the first permanent courthouse in the Eastern Goldfields), with a working gold-battery model, a camel wagon and mining displays; the Southern Cross page says it is open daily.
objection: A small local museum; one board.

name: Pathways to Wave Rock
reason: Not a place: a 760 km self-drive trail through Wheatbelt towns to Wave Rock; Wave Rock and the towns are the spots.
objection: None.

name: Merredin WWII Army Hospital Sites
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Merredin page names 'the interpreted sites of the World War II Army Hospital' and a 'World War II Sites in Merredin' listing; an outdoor heritage site, not a working hospital.
objection: One board only (the product page URL tried returned 404); interpreted ruins and signs may be a short stop, and Merredin's Military Museum may cover the same story (possible near-duplicate).
